title: The Inheritance
premise: Old Arn Voss is dead and the house on Mill Lane is the only thing he left. The bank wants its money in three days and a developer wants the land. The family, the lodgers and the neighbours who half-lived there must decide what happens to it.

socialQuestion.text: Does loyalty keep people holding on to a thing that is costing them?
socialQuestion.hypothesis: Citizens with loyal > 0.7 will choose 'keep' at a markedly higher rate than citizens with loyal < 0.4, even after the roof is found to be rotten.

fingerprint.setting: family house in a small market town, present day
fingerprint.pressure: bank deadline + a developer's offer + a contested will
fingerprint.dynamic: sentiment vs. solvency; who gets to decide for a family

beliefs.text: a developer will pay double for the land
the roof beams are rotten and the house is worth almost nothing
the will that leaves everything to the eldest was altered

events.headline: A man in a good coat buys a round and asks about Mill Lane.
events.text: He says a company he works for would pay double the bank's figure. Cash. This week.

events.headline: The surveyor comes down from the attic shaking his head.
events.text: The main beams are soft. He will not put a number on it in front of the family.

events.headline: A second will, handwritten, turns up in the notary's post.
events.text: It is dated a month before Arn died. It divides everything three ways.

events.headline: The bank's letter: the mortgage is called in. Seventy-two hours from the funeral.
events.text: Pay it, sell it, or the bank takes it and sells it for them.

events.headline: The man in the good coat has checked out of The Crown.
events.text: He left no number. The landlord says he asked about two other houses on the way out.

events.headline: The notary lays the papers on the kitchen table. Sign by dawn or the bank signs for you.
events.text: Three documents. One sells, one refinances, one divides. Nobody leaves the room.

ending.prompt: The papers are signed at hour 72.
